Seo.introBody: WorldTime is a free world clock, time zone converter, and meeting planner. Compare the local time across cities and time zones, find the best hours to schedule international meetings, and share time selections with automatic daylight saving time (DST) support.

faq.q: How do I compare the time in two cities?
faq.a: Add the cities with the search box and the time grid shows every hour side by side, with the live offset between them.

faq.q: Does WorldTime handle daylight saving time?
faq.a: Yes. Daylight saving transitions are detected automatically for each city, so the offset is correct on spring-forward and fall-back days too.

faq.q: How do I find the best time for an international meeting?
faq.a: Add everyone's cities, then use the color heatmap to find hours where no one is asleep. Select a slot to export it to your calendar.
Yes, WorldTime is completely free, runs in the browser, and does not require an account.

faq.q: Is the time shown in real time?
faq.a: The current time and converter tables update live in your browser every minute.

Help.step1Body: Use the search box to add every place you're coordinating across.

About.title: About WorldTime
About.metaDescription: How WorldTime calculates local time, offsets, and daylight saving from IANA — plus features and use cases.
About.lead: WorldTime is a free world clock, time-zone converter, and meeting planner. It is built for reading overlap at a glance — no account, no paywall.
About.howBody: Each city is mapped to one IANA time zone. Offsets and calendar dates are computed with Luxon from that zone at a given instant, in the browser and in the HTML we send to crawlers.
About.dataBody: Zone rules come from the IANA Time Zone Database (tzdb), the same dataset used by operating systems. We do not scrape other clock websites.
About.dstBody: DST is taken from the zone, not from a URL label. A slug like EST--PST is a search alias; in summer America/New_York is EDT. The live abbreviation on each page is authoritative.
About.privacyBlurb: Privacy: we do not require an account. Details

Privacy.title: Privacy
Privacy.metaDescription: WorldTime privacy notes: no account, city lists stay in your browser.
paragraphs: WorldTime does not require an account and does not run a user database for the clock itself.
Cities you add, theme, and display settings are stored in your browser (localStorage) so the grid can restore on the next visit. Clearing site data removes them.
The site is a static/SSR web app. Times are calculated on your device and on our servers from IANA zone data; we do not sell personal profiles.
If you install the app as a PWA, the service worker caches pages for offline use on that device only.
